newsitem.title: FINLAND: GOVT WANTS MERITA MANAGEMENT OPTIONS CHANGED - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: GOVT WANTS MERITA MANAGEMENT OPTIONS CHANGED - PAPER.

text.p: The finance minstry is in talks with banking group Merita Oy, demanding changes to its planned management option scheme, business daily Kauppalehti reported on Tuesday.

"Our starting point is that the bonds with warrants should have a clause that possible options profits could not be taken before (the state) capital certificates have been repaid," Kauppalehti quoted finance ministry legislation director Pekka Laajanen as saying. He was leading the talks, it said.
The state is Merita's largest owner and has granted capital certificates worth 3.5 billion markka to the banking group.
